{{center block/s}}</noinclude><section begin="ode1" />Some hull (the grain); some take it from the mortar;{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Some sift it; some tread it.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
It is rattling in the dishes;{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
It is distilled, and the steam floats about.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
We consult<ref>That is, we divine about the day, and choose the officers to take part in the service.</ref>; we observe the rites of purification;{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
We take southernwood and offer it with the fat;{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
We sacrifice a ram to the spirit of the path<ref>A sacrifice was offered to the {{anchor+|spirit of the road}} on commencing a journey, and we see here that it was offered also in connexion with the king's going to the [[w:Ancestral temple|ancestral temple]] or the border altar.</ref>;{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
We offer roast flesh and broiled:—{{lb}}And
thus introduce the coming year<ref>It does not appear clearly what sacrifices the poet had in view here. I think they must be all those in which the [[Portal:Zhou dynasty|kings of ''K''âu]] appeared as the principals or sacrificers. The concluding line is understood to intimate that the kings were not to forget that a prosperous agriculture was the foundation of their prosperity.</ref>.

We load the stands with the offerings,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
The stands both of wood and of earthenware.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
As soon as the fragrance ascends,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
God, well pleased, smells the sweet savour.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Fragrant it is, and in its due season<ref>In this stanza we have the peculiar honour paid to [[w:Hou Ji|Hâu-''k''î]] by his descendants at one of the great border sacrifices to God,—the same to which the [[Sacred Books of the East/Volume 3/The Shih/Odes of the Temple and the Altar/The Sacrificial Odes of Kâu/Decade 1/Ode 10|last ode in the first decade of the Sacrificial Odes of ''K''âu]] belongs.</ref>.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Hâu-''k''î founded our sacrifices,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
And no one, we presume, has given occasion for blame or regret in regard to them,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Down to the present day.
{{center block/e}}
